scope: Working composition principles. Implementation status describes the current arranger, not universal musical truth.

rules.title: Give the piece an identity
rules.principle: Establish a recognisable melodic, rhythmic, harmonic or textural idea and make its intended presentation audible.
rules.rationale: A listener needs landmarks to recognise relationships and returns.
rules.exception: An intentionally evolving texture can use timbre or process as its identity instead of a singable hook.
rules.implementation: Seeded contours and recurring section material; no independently stored or pinnable motif.
rules.plannedLevers: Audition and pin hooks; record motif identity and landmarks

rules.title: Develop without losing the connection
rules.principle: Choose whether each phrase establishes, varies, develops or recalls earlier material.
rules.rationale: Purposeful transformation creates continuity while changing the musical argument.
rules.exception: Exact repetition can be the right choice for dance, meditation or participation; novelty is optional.
rules.implementation: Limited phrase variation and recurring contours; no transformation provenance.
rules.plannedLevers: Phrase function; transformation type; landmark preservation

rules.title: Make phrase and section roles audible
rules.principle: Give phrases a relationship and sections a function beyond their labels.
rules.rationale: Statement, response, departure and arrival help listeners understand scale and direction.
rules.exception: Four two-bar phrases are our pop default; alternative forms can choose other lengths.
rules.implementation: Four two-bar verse/chorus phrases, a bridge and varied intro; fixed family of forms.
rules.plannedLevers: Prechorus; breakdown; suite form; explicit phrase intentions

rules.title: Give harmony direction and duration
rules.principle: Plan harmonic spans, voice leading and arrivals in relation to the motif and form.
rules.rationale: A chord list alone does not specify pacing, expectation or melodic meaning.
rules.exception: Static harmony and unresolved colour can be intentional; tonic closure is not required at every phrase.
rules.implementation: Progression choices, substitutions, section contrast and voice-led voicings; chords remain bar-sized.
rules.currentLevers: Chord progression; custom chords; progression variation; section contrast
rules.plannedLevers: Harmonic rhythm; held chords; local key; cadence targets

rules.title: Build groove through relationships
rules.principle: Coordinate metre, subdivision, accents, durations and deliberate timing between roles.
rules.rationale: Groove depends on patterned interactions, not a tempo number or independent jitter.
rules.exception: Straight and quantised performances are legitimate; swing is a style choice.
rules.implementation: Beat templates and offbeat delay; no compound-metre model or role-specific timing curves.

rules.title: Allocate attention and leave useful space
rules.principle: Give each layer a role and coordinate its density, entrances and responses with the foreground.
rules.rationale: Arbitrary layers can mask the hook; silence and answering gestures make relationships audible.
rules.exception: Counterpoint and deliberate dense textures can overlap; universal non-overlap is not a rule.
rules.implementation: Section participation probabilities and fixed answer slots; parts do not generally react to actual lead occupancy.
rules.currentLevers: Instrument layers; per-section presence; occurrence overrides
rules.plannedLevers: Foreground priority; density budget; actual-rest responses

rules.title: Write for the instrument
rules.principle: Choose register, articulation, feasible gestures and transitions appropriate to the part.
rules.rationale: A sampled instrument does not automatically supply idiomatic performance.
rules.exception: Unusual ranges and techniques can be deliberate choices with an explicit override.
rules.implementation: Selectable SoundFont instruments and octave/gain/velocity controls; limited writing constraints.
rules.plannedLevers: Playable range; strumming; bowing; breath and transition models

rules.title: Shape a journey across the piece
rules.principle: Plan changes in energy, tension, stability and density separately, with meaningful departures and returns.
rules.rationale: A loud stable passage and a quiet tense passage have different functions.
rules.exception: A sustained mood or process can be the goal; every work need not tell a dramatic story.
rules.implementation: Section harmony, intro build, presence and outro choices; no explicit narrative-intent plan.
rules.currentLevers: Section contrast; intro variation; layer presence
rules.plannedLevers: Independent energy/tension arcs; delayed recall; transition intent

rules.title: Perform phrases with intent
rules.principle: Relate stress, dynamics, attack, duration, breathing and timing to the phrase's role.
rules.rationale: Expression comes from coherent gestures and contrasts rather than arbitrary errors.
rules.exception: Mechanical articulation can be a deliberate aesthetic; expressive exaggeration is optional.
rules.implementation: Note velocities and limited phrase/section shaping; no general performance-phrase model.
rules.plannedLevers: Phrase stress; articulation; tempo curves; controlled breathing

rules.title: Finish within the promise
rules.principle: Reserve a complete audible outro and its release within the requested length ceiling; finish early when necessary.
rules.rationale: An arbitrary cutoff breaks the intended phrase and the user's duration contract.
rules.exception: A deliberate abrupt stop is valid when planned and rendered as the ending.
rules.implementation: The arranger reserves an outro and completes sections within the ceiling, with fade, cadence, tag or coordinated stop.

rules.title: Give the user independent musical choices
rules.principle: Explain what each lever changes and preserves; expose related levers progressively.
rules.rationale: Useful authorship requires controllable decisions, understandable interactions and comparisons.
rules.exception: A beginner can choose a coherent recipe without adjusting every parameter.
rules.implementation: Independent harmony, groove, instrument and presence settings, score saves and exports; no hook/section pinning.
rules.currentLevers: Genre; settings controls; local saves; import/export
rules.plannedLevers: Pin material; regenerate selected sections; compare the same score

rules.title: Ground recipes in works and periods
rules.principle: Describe artist-related combinations using named recordings, dates, evidence and explicit limits.
rules.rationale: Artists change over time and across collaborators; one slider setting cannot represent a whole career.
rules.exception: A broad genre recipe is useful when labelled as a starting point rather than a measured artist profile.
rules.implementation: The research provides case studies; no artist timeline, measured artist factors or generated artist demonstrations are available.
rules.plannedLevers: Source-backed work/period comparisons; original mechanism demonstrations

rules.title: Evaluate and revise honestly
rules.principle: Verify event-level promises, listen to controlled comparisons and version changes to rules and composition separately.
rules.rationale: Reproducibility establishes what happened; listening helps assess whether the intended effect worked.
rules.exception: Criteria depend on musical intent, and listener disagreement should be recorded.
rules.implementation: Deterministic tests and saved scores exist; blinded musical listening comparisons remain planned.
rules.plannedLevers: Blind comparisons; style-specific rubric; saved rule provenance

history.changes: Initial thirteen contextual rules, linked to thesis revision 0.1. Separates current capabilities from planned levers.
